text:
anya (sales): Heads-up: PioneerAPI migration POC starts tomorrow. Customer asks: swap Pioneer endpoints for Redwood without changing search+extract UX. They care about token parity, billing mapping (their per-call bundles), and a short security write-up for procurement. @diego can you take the lead for tech presales?

diego (solutions): Got it. Draft checklist: 1) adapter contract mapping (req/resp fields) 2) tokenization diff sample 3) prompt normalization rules (stop sequences/defaults) 4) error semantics & retry mapping 5) A/B harness + parity metrics 6) pricing mapping examples 7) procurement security blurb.

mei (eng): Adapter plan: lightweight proxy that accepts Pioneer payloads, rewrites to Redwood API, and returns wrapped responses. We'll do header mapping, default param translation, and token normalization. Short example:```bash
# client -> adapter: POST /pioneer/v2/query {"q":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":350}
# adapter -> redwood: POST /v1/generate {"input":"<PROMPT>","max_total_tokens":350, "stop":["\n\n"]}
```We saw an initial token delta of ~+9% on a 150-sample set; we'll run a 200-sample run.

rana (security): Procurement needs: EU data residency confirmation, KMS options, audit log delivery, and evidence of SOC2. Quick answers: we can pin EU region for Private/Dedicated, CMK via AWS KMS supported, audit logs exportable (S3/syslog). HSM via partner on request (legal+procurement). Send me their questionnaire highlights.

jai (sales-eng): Pricing: Pioneer sells flat bundles (calls). Options: A) token-equivalent pricing with a delta adjustment B) flat-call equivalent using measured average tokens per call C) migration credit month to offset delta. I'll prepare example invoices for 40k calls/mo assuming +9% token delta.

zoe (cs): Canary ops: start with synthetic parity tests (same prompts/seed), then 4% live traffic with auto-failback to Pioneer on >=2 errors/3m. Capture diffs: length delta, missing fields in extracted JSON, parsing errors. We'll provide dashboards for parity metrics.

mei (eng): Response deltas sources: tokenizer vocab, default sampling (Pioneer default temp=0.6), and stop handling. Mitigations: set explicit temp=0.0 for deterministic POC, add explicit stop tokens, and run post-normalize (trim whitespace/punctuation). We'll include a small shim to adjust token counts before billing.

diego (solutions): Eval harness plan: node script that calls both endpoints, records tokens and outputs, then computes metrics: token_delta, exact_match_rate, structured_field_f1, length_delta. We'll produce a JSONL per prompt for triage.

rana (security): Action: I'll draft procurement blurb and answer their highlighted questions by tomorrow noon. Need the questionnaire PDF and the specific highlighted lines.

anya (sales): Uploaded questionnaire PDF and flagged sections: EU residency, HSM proof, retention for logs, and SLA for POC (>=99.5%).

jai (sales-eng): I'll include a recommended migration credit (20% first-month usage) in pricing scenarios to mitigate delta risk.

ci-bot: Canary scheduled: pioneer-adapter -> canary-2026-03-27T07:30Z (4% traffic). CI checks: unit tests + parity harness.

diego (solutions): Owners & deadlines: 1) 200-sample tokenizer run -> diego (EOD) 2) adapter stub & mapping doc -> mei (tomorrow 09:30) 3) procurement answers -> rana + legal (tomorrow noon) 4) pricing scenarios -> jai (tomorrow COB) 5) parity harness -> diego + mei (initial by day 1 of POC) 6) canary runbook & failback -> zoe (pre-canary).

anya (sales): Quick sync 08:45 tomorrow for 10m. Ping here if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
